# Env

```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(dplyr)
    library(ComplexHeatmap)
    library(ggplot2)
    library(patchwork)
    library(ggrepel)
    library(ggpubr)
})

theme_md_classic <- function() {
    theme_classic(
        base_size = 6, 
        base_family = "ArialMT",
        base_line_size = 0.25,
        base_rect_size = 0.25
    ) %+replace% theme(
        axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
        axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black"),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 6),  # was size 8 in other notebooks?
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 8),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 6),
        complete = TRUE
    )
}

theme_md_bw <- function() {
    theme_bw(
        base_size = 6, 
        base_family = "ArialMT",
        base_line_size = 0.25,
        base_rect_size = 0.25
    ) %+replace% theme(
        axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
        axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black"),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 6),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 8),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 6),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, color = "black"),
        complete = TRUE
    )
}
```

## Utilities

### CPM normalization

```{r}
# rows are features, columns are samples
cpm <- function(mat) {
    t(1e6 * t(mat) / colSums(mat))
}
```

### Z-scoring

not used

```{r}
# z-score each row in matrix
scale_rows <- function(m) {
    t(scale(t(m)))
}
```

# Multiome cluster distances in panel vs. HVGs

To answer reviewer question about "if they would produce similar clustering"
or whatever

## in just gene-expression space

i guess first i'll just do in gene expression space

```{r}
multi_mats_for_sets %>% 
    lapply(log1p) %>% 
    lapply(t) %>% 
    lapply(dist) -> 
    multi_mats_for_sets_dists
```

```{r}
multi_mats_for_sets_dists[[1]] %>% as.matrix %>% .[1:3,1:3]
```

### all clusters

```{r}
multi_mats_for_sets_dists %>% 
    lapply(as.vector) %>%
    do.call(cbind, .) %>% 
    as.data.frame %>% 
    setNames(c("HVGs", "panel")) ->
    df_gsets_gexp_dist
```

```{r}
ggplot(df_gsets_gexp_dist, aes(HVGs, panel)) +
    # geom_point() + 
    geom_hex(bins=100) + 
    scale_fill_viridis_c(trans="log10") + 
    geom_smooth(method="lm") + 
    ggpubr::stat_cor() + 
    labs(
        title = "Cluster Pairwise Distances\nin Gene Expression Space",
        x = "4k HVGs", y = "300 Gene Spatial Panel", fill="Cluster Pairs"
    ) + 
    theme_md_classic()
```

R=0.98

```{r}
ggsave(
    file.path(pdir_plots, "scatter_genesets_cl_pairwise_gexp_dist_all_cl.pdf"),

)
```

#### Mantel test

```{r}
all_cl_mantel <- vegan::mantel(
    multi_mats_for_sets_dists$HVGs,
    multi_mats_for_sets_dists$panel,
    method = "pearson",
    permutations = 5e3
)
```

kind of pointless, just a significance test on what i already have, and the
p-val adds nothing

### just neurons vs. non-neurons?

```{r}
obs %>% 
    tibble::rownames_to_column("cluster") %>% 
    (function(x) split(x$cluster, x$Subcortex_Class_v4=="Nonneuron")) %>% 
    (function(x) {
        stopifnot(identical(names(x), c("FALSE", "TRUE")))
        x
    }) %>% 
    setNames(c("Neurons", "Nonneurons")) %>% 
    lapply(function(cl) {
        multi_mats_for_sets_dists %>% 
            lapply(as.matrix) %>% 
            lapply(function(x) x[cl, cl]) %>% 
            lapply(function(x) x[upper.tri(x)]) %>% 
            do.call(cbind, .) %>% 
            as.data.frame %>% 
            setNames(c("HVGs", "panel"))
    }) %>% 
    Map(function(x, nm) mutate(x, grping = nm), ., names(.)) %>% 
    unname %>% 
    do.call(rbind, .) ->
    df_gsets_gexp_dist_by_neur_vs_glia
```

```{r}
ggplot(df_gsets_gexp_dist_by_neur_vs_glia, aes(HVGs, panel)) +
    facet_wrap(~grping) + 
    geom_hex(bins=100) + 
    scale_fill_viridis_c(trans="log10") + 
    geom_smooth(method="lm") + 
    ggpubr::stat_cor() + 
    labs(
        title = "Cluster Pairwise Distances\nin Gene Expression Space",
        x = "4k HVGs", y = "300 Gene Spatial Panel", fill="Cluster Pairs"
    ) + 
    theme_md_bw()
```


```{r}
ggsave(
    file.path(pdir_plots, "scatter_genesets_cl_pairwise_gexp_dist_split_neur_glia.pdf"),
```

### make one big combined plot

### Get correlations across all groups

#### split by group

want to see the distribution

```{r}
obs %>% 
    tibble::rownames_to_column("cluster") %>% 
    (function(x) split(x$cluster, x$Subcortex_Group_v4)) %>% 
    lapply(function(cl) {
        multi_mats_for_sets_dists %>% 
            lapply(as.matrix) %>% 
            lapply(function(x) x[cl, cl]) %>% 
            lapply(function(x) x[upper.tri(x)]) %>% # no redundant or self-self
            do.call(cbind, .) %>% 
            as.data.frame %>% 
            setNames(c("HVGs", "panel"))
    }) %>% 
    Map(function(x, nm) mutate(x, Group = nm), ., names(.)) %>% 
    unname %>% 
    do.call(rbind, .) ->
    df_gsets_gexp_dist_by_group
```

```{r}
# do for any Group with 3+ clusters:
# (1 is impossible, 2 is R=1 so that's cheating)
df_gsets_gexp_dist_by_group %>% 
    # only look at Groups with at least 3+ clusters
    filter(
        Group %in% { table(obs$Subcortex_Group_v4) %>% .[.>2] %>% names }
    ) %>% 
    group_by(Group) %>% 
    summarize(cor = cor(HVGs, panel)) %>% 
    .$cor %>% 
    summary
#   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
# 0.7942  0.9300  0.9499  0.9447  0.9715  1.0000 

df_gsets_gexp_dist_by_group %>% 
    # only look at Groups with at least 2+ clusters
    filter(
        Group %in% { table(obs$Subcortex_Group_v4) %>% .[.>2] %>% names }
    ) %>% 
    group_by(Group) %>% 
    summarize(cor = cor(HVGs, panel)) %>% 
    .$cor %>% 
    sd
# [1] 0.04030681
```

# Check on panel gene variance

like, the reviewer wants to know "how many of the genes are differentially
expressed between the clusters"

```{r}
var_df <- rbind(
    tibble::rownames_to_column(
        data.frame(
            var = apply(log1p(rna_by_cl_cpm[panel_gns, ]), 1, var), 
            set = "Spatial Panel"
        ),
        "gene"
    ),
    tibble::rownames_to_column(
        data.frame(
            var = apply(log1p(rna_by_cl_cpm[hvgs, ]), 1, var), 
            set = "4k HVGs"
        ),
        "gene"
    )
)
```


```{r}
var_df %>% 
    ggplot(
        aes(var, color = set, fill = set)
    ) + 
    geom_density(alpha=0.25) + 
    # scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::math_format(2^.x)) + 
    labs(
        x = "gene variance across clusters",
        color = "gene set",
        fill = "gene set"
    ) + 
    theme_md_classic() + 
    theme(legend.key.size = unit(3, "mm"))
```

```{r}
ggsave(
    file.path(pdir_plots, "panel_vs_hvg_gene_variance.pdf"),
    width=80, height=40, units="mm"
)
```

```{r}
var_df %>% 
    ggplot(
        aes(var, set)
    ) + 
    geom_boxplot() + 
    labs(

        y = NULL
    ) +

```

```{r}
        var = apply(log1p(rna_by_cl_cpm), 1, var)
    ),
    "gene"
) %>% 
    arrange(var) %>% 
    mutate(rank_pct = rank(var) / length(var))
```

```{r}
    mutate(filter(var_all, gene %in% panel_gns), set = "Spatial Panel")

    group_by(set) %>% 
    summarize(median(rank_pct)) %>% 
    print.data.frame

# 2 Spatial Panel        0.9712885
```

## (!) Recreate GE_RegionNT for this heatmap

See notebook `combined_analysis` for eRegulon analysis.

*Get "rg_cl": set of regionally localized neuronal clusters*

For many (but not all) analyses, we will only use clusters that are spatially
localized to an anatomical structure.

```{r}
rg_cl <- rownames(filter(
    obs,
    Subcortex_Class_v4 != "Nonneuron",
    Cluster_Dominant_Region != "Multi"
))
```


*Make NT_MSN to separate MSNs*

Separate the MSNs from other GABA neurons.

```{r}
obs$NT_MSN <- obs$Cluster_NT
obs$NT_MSN[grep("MSN", obs$Subcortex_Group_v4)] <- "MSN"
```

*Add RegionNT (w/ separated MSNs)*

```{r}
obs$RegionNT <- paste0(obs$Cluster_Dominant_Region, "_", obs$NT_MSN)
```

*Add GE derivation annotations*

```{r}
ge_groups <- list(
    CGE = c(
        "LAMP5-CXCL14 GABA",
        "NDNF GABA",
        "PAX6 GABA",
        "PBX3 GABA",
        "VIP GABA"
    ),
    MGE = c(
        "CTX PVALB GABA",
        "CTX PVALB Chandelier GABA",
        "GPin-BF Cholinergic GABA",
        "LAMP5-LHX6 GABA", 
        "STR Cholinergic GABA",
        "STR FS PTHLH-PVALB GABA",
        "STR LYPD6-RSPO2 GABA",
        "STR SST-ADARB2 GABA",
        "STR SST-CHODL GABA",
        "STR SST-RSPO2 GABA",
        "STR TAC3-PLPP4 GABA",
        "STRd Cholinergic GABA",
        "STR-BF TAC3-PLPP4-LHX8 GABA"
    ),
    LGE = c(
        "AMY-STR ITC-NUDAP MSN",
        "GPe MEIS2-SOX6 GABA", # was "GP MEIS2-SOX6 GABA" in preprint
        "OT D1 ICj",
        "STRd D1 Matrix MSN",
        "STRd D1 Striosome MSN",
        "STR D1D2 Hybrid MSN", # was "STRd D1D2 Hybrid MSN" in preprint
        "STRd D2 Matrix MSN",
        "STRd D2 StrioMat Hybrid MSN",
        "STRd D2 Striosome MSN",
        "STRv D1 MSN",
        "STRv D2 MSN"
    )
)
stopifnot(all(unlist(ge_groups) %in% obs$Subcortex_Group_v4))
```

*Mutate obs*

```{r}
nm_map <- setNames(
    rep(names(ge_groups), lengths(ge_groups)),
    unname(unlist(ge_groups))
)

obs$GE <- ifelse(
    obs$Subcortex_Group_v4 %in% names(nm_map),
    nm_map[obs$Subcortex_Group_v4],
    NA
)
```


*Make GE_RegionNT*

The column `GE_RegionNT` will be NA for everything not GE-derived. In hindsight
I could have dealt with this more elegantly, but it's slightly convenient in
many plots to just show the GE-derived cells and nothing else.

```{r}
obs <- mutate(
    obs,
    GE_RegionNT = ifelse(
        is.na(GE),
        NA,
        paste0(GE, "_", RegionNT)
    )
)
```

*Also make complete GE_RegionNT_Complete*

Unlike `GE_RegionNT`, this won't be NA for non-GE-derived, but will instead
use `RegionNT` unless there's a value for `GE_RegionNT`.

So when this variable is used, all RegionNT will be shown (with GE-derived
cells divided out).

```{r}
obs$GE_RegionNT_Complete <- ifelse(
    is.na(obs$GE_RegionNT),
    as.character(obs$RegionNT),
    as.character(obs$GE_RegionNT)
)
```

```{r}
obs$GE_RegionNT_Complete_Glia <- ifelse(
    obs$Subcortex_Class_v4 == "Nonneuron",
    obs$Subcortex_Group_v4,
    obs$GE_RegionNT_Complete
)
```

# Spatial vs. multiome metacell correlations

Pearons's R of log1p(CPM) cluster-level pseudobulk (assigned spatial clusters
vs. multiome clusters).

Rows for spatial metacell, and columns for multiome metacells.

```{r}
pb_cor <- cor(log1p(matched_pb_mats$spatial), log1p(matched_pb_mats$multiome))
stopifnot(all(rownames(pb_cor) == colnames(pb_cor)))
```

## couple quick checks

```{r}
# (also should be ~impossible but will check for any ties)
# > pb_cor %>% apply(1, function(x) length(which(x == max(x))) > 1) %>% unlist %>% any 
# [1] FALSE

# most common hits? [are any multiome clusters soaking up correlations?]
pb_cor %>% apply(1, which.max) %>% 
    colnames(pb_cor)[.] %>% 
    table %>% 
    sort(TRUE) %>% 
    head(10)
# cluster_217   cluster_65  cluster_750  cluster_848  cluster_187  cluster_681 cluster_1742 
#          14           12           11           10            8            8            7 
# cluster_207 cluster_1129 cluster_1424 
#           7            6            6 

## a little bit but nothing totally wild; but what are those clusters?
pb_cor %>% apply(1, which.max) %>% 
    colnames(pb_cor)[.] %>% 
    table %>% 
    sort(TRUE) %>% 
    head(10) %>% 
    names %>% 
    (function(x) obs[x, "Subcortex_Group_v4"])
 # [1] "VP-MG Glut"              "STRd D1 Matrix MSN"      "LGmc-LGpc Glut"          "Microglia"              
 # [5] "STR FS PTHLH-PVALB GABA" "Astro-NT NN"             "DG Glut"                 "VLN Glut"               
 # [9] "L6 CT CTX-PArCx Glut"    "L2-3 Pir-ERC Glut" 


### how many match their namesake?
pb_cor %>% apply(1, which.max) %>% 
    (function(x) data.frame(spatial = names(x), multiome = colnames(pb_cor)[unname(x)])) %>% 
    mutate(match = spatial==multiome) %>% 
    .$match %>% 
    sum
# [1] 1157 # out of 1620
```

so 72% of the time the best match by correlation is the namesake

```{r}
pb_cor %>% apply(1, which.max) %>% 
    (function(x) data.frame(spatial = names(x), multiome = colnames(pb_cor)[unname(x)])) %>% 
    mutate(match = spatial==multiome) %>% 
    filter(!match) %>% 
    (function(x) {
        cbind(x, obs[x$spatial, ][, c(
            "Subcortex_Class_v4", "Subcortex_Group_v4", "Cluster_v4_size", "Cluster_Dominant_Region"
```

## get dataframe of top couple hits and namesake

```{r}
pb_cor %>% 
    apply(1, sort, TRUE, simplify = FALSE) %>% 
    Map(function(x, qry) {
        data.frame(
            query = qry,
            top_hit = names(x)[1],
            top_cor = unname(x)[1],
            second_hit = names(x)[2],
            second_cor = unname(x)[2],
            namesake_rank = which(names(x)==qry),
            namesake_cor  = x[qry]
        )
    }, ., names(.)) %>% 
    bind_rows %>% 
    `rownames<-`(NULL) %>% 
    (function(x) {
        x$query_group <- obs[x$query, "Subcortex_Group_v4"]
        x$query_class <- obs[x$query, "Subcortex_Class_v4"]
        x$query_region <- obs[x$query, "Cluster_Dominant_Region"]
        x$top_hit_group <- obs[x$top_hit, "Subcortex_Group_v4"]
        x$top_hit_class <- obs[x$top_hit, "Subcortex_Class_v4"]
        x$top_hit_region <- obs[x$top_hit, "Cluster_Dominant_Region"]
        x
    }) -> 
    df_metacell_sim
```

### aggregate matching by group

what about group matching (by group)?

```{r}
df_metacell_sim %>% 
    split(., .$query_group) %>%
    lapply(function(x) {
        # get top mismatched group
        top_miss <- table(x$top_hit_group) %>% 
            sort(TRUE) %>% 
            .[!names(.)==x$query_group]
        
        if (length(top_miss)==0) {
            top_miss <- c("none" = 0)
        } else {
            top_miss <- top_miss[1]
        }
        
        data.frame(
            assigned_group = unique(x$query_group),
            n_clusts = nrow(x),
            frac_cl_mtch_grp = round(
                sum(x$top_hit_group == x$query_group) / nrow(x),
                3
            ),
            top_wrng_grp = names(top_miss),
            top_wrng_grp_frac = round(unname(top_miss)/nrow(x), 3)
        )
    }) %>% 
    suppressWarnings %>% 
    bind_rows %>% 
    mutate(top_wrng_grp = sub("none", "", top_wrng_grp)) ->
    df_metacell_sim_by_group
```

so this is looking at groups whose assigned cells can have multiple different
groups be more similar:

```{r}
df_metacell_sim_by_group %>% 
    filter(frac_cl_mtch_grp + top_wrng_grp_frac < 1) %>% 
    arrange(frac_cl_mtch_grp + top_wrng_grp_frac) %>% 
    print.data.frame
```
